subject: Joint success plan & contract clauses for Nimbus pilot
messages:
From: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@nimbus.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Joint success plan & contract clauses for Nimbus pilot

Connor / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the observability hooks. We want to move forward with a 90-day pilot to validate: 1) integration with our API gateway, 2) live A/B on our customer-facing recommender, and 3) perf/quality baselines for your LLM variants.

High level asks from our side:
- MAP: a short joint success plan with milestones and acceptance gates (integration ready, live A/B, quality sign-off).
- Commercial: a pilot commit for the first 90 days (we expect a ramp, not steady-state usage). We need clarity on how pricing and discounts will apply during ramp and what true-up mechanics look like if we exceed committed levels.
- Contract redlines: our procurement will push back on open-ended true-ups and any language that allows retroactive price increases. Can you share standard language around true-ups, price protection, and a clear definition of "billable usage"?

I've attached our draft MAP (RDW-NIMBUS_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a short usage forecast. If we can land on MAP milestones and the commercial levers this week, we can get procurement engaged.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Monroe
Head of Data & ML, Nimbus Systems

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Joint success plan & contract clauses for Nimbus pilot

Lisa — thanks, excited to move forward. Quick thoughts and proposed defaults so we can converge quickly:

MAP / Eval plan (proposed):
- Week 0–2: Integration smoke tests (API keys, network, KV caching).
- Week 3–5: Shadow traffic + internal QA.
- Week 6–9: Live A/B at 10–25% traffic; collect quality/latency metrics.
- Week 10–12: Ramp to target capacity and finalize acceptance criteria.

Commercial mechanics (proposal):
- Pilot commit: a 90-day committed token volume expressed as monthly tranches (example: M1=25%, M2=50%, M3=100% of target).
- Pricing: list price then commit-discount bands. Discounts apply to billable usage up to committed volume; overage billed at list with a quarterly true-up.
- True-up cadence: quarterly settlement for over-usage beyond committed volumes. We can add a cap on back-billing to limit surprise (e.g., 1.5x of monthly expected overage in the quarter).
- Price protection: 12 months from execution on negotiated unit price; after that list price applies unless re-negotiated.

Key open item: definition of "billable usage" — Redwood measures tokens generated + tokens consumed in prompts (net tokens). If Nimbus prefers per-request or per-inference-unit billing, we can map equivalence but need a deterministic formula in the SOW.

Next steps: I can send an updated MAP (v3) that includes the ramp tranches and suggested pricing bands. Does Nimbus have a preferred cap on true-up back-billing or a maximum lookback window your procurement teams insist on?

I cc'd Neha for legal/contract language.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-NIMBUS_MAP_v3.xlsx (proposed MAP with tranches)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@nimbus.io>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Joint success plan & contract clauses for Nimbus pilot

Lisa / Connor — looping in a few contract defaults we typically use and our suggested redline language. High-level positions:

1) Billable usage definition: "Billable Usage" = total tokens received by the model + tokens generated by the model for inference requests from Customer. Test traffic (identified in the MAP and flagged in logs) will be excluded from billable usage for the length of the pilot. Any alternative metering (per-inference or per-API-call) must be explicitly enumerated in the SOW.

2) True-ups: Quarterly true-up for usage above committed volumes. We agree to a 90-day lookback. Redwood proposes no retroactive price increases for past usage; back-billing limited to actual usage delta. To limit surprise, we can accept a back-billing cap of 20% of committed quarterly volume for the pilot period.

3) Price protection: Fixed unit price for the first 12 months from the Effective Date for volumes covered by committed tranches. After 12 months, pricing reverts to list unless both parties agree in writing.

4) Ramp & discounts: Commit bands with tiered discounts (to be reflected in the MAP). Example banding is fine-grained in the attached Redwood-Standard-GSA-Clauses_redlines.pdf.

If Nimbus counters on the back-billing cap / lookback window we can be flexible; let us know procurement's minimum acceptable terms. I'll prepare a redline PDF and an inline summary for your legal team to review.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: Redwood-Standard-GSA-Clauses_redlines.pdf (redline excerpt)

From: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@nimbus.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nimbus.io>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Joint success plan & contract clauses for Nimbus pilot

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clarity. A few counterpoints from procurement/prod:

- True-up cap: our procurement wants back-billing limited to 10% per quarter for the pilot (we can agree to higher caps for multi-year renewals, but the pilot needs predictability).
- Lookback window: 60 days is the team's sweet spot; 90 days is workable but not preferred.
- Price protection: 12 months ok. Can we add a clause that any list price increases must be notified 60 days in advance and won't apply to committed volumes for the protection period?
- Definition of billable usage: we'll accept token-based metering but request a deterministic conversion for historical metrics (we'll provide a 30-day sample of API calls so we can reconcile).

Ramp suggestion: M1=30% of target commit, M2=60%, M3=100% — we want a softer ramp to reduce risk. Acceptance criteria we care about: p95 latency < 200ms for production model variant, end-to-end error rate < 0.5%, and model-quality delta vs baseline model < 1% in our A/B metric (CTR lift).

If Redwood can accept: back-billing cap 10% (pilot only), 60-day lookback, 60-day notice for list price increases, and include conversion table for token-per-call mapping in the SOW, we'll push to procurement this week. I've attached our usage sample and a suggested small redline packet.

-Lisa

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Monroe <lisa.monroe@nimbus.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Joint success plan & contract clauses for Nimbus pilot

Lisa — thanks for the clear asks. From a commercial ops perspective we can work toward your ramp and most of the procurement asks with two clarifications:

1) Discounting model: we'll reflect commit-tier discounts in the MAP. Example (illustrative):
- 0–50% commit band: 0% discount (list)
- 51–200% commit band: 12% discount on committed volume
- >200%: standard overage rates at list
(We can tweak the bands based on your expected steady-state numbers.)

2) True-up mechanics and caps: for the pilot we can accept a 10% cap on retroactive billing as long as Nimbus shares the 30-day sample data within 48 hours of execution and we mutually agree on the conversion mapping. For operational simplicity, the true-up will be invoiced in the quarter following the over-usage discovery; the lookback window will be 60 days for pilot billing adjustments.

3) Test traffic exclusion: we'll exclude flagged test traffic from billing during the pilot; the MAP must include how test traffic is flagged and who has access to the traffic logs.

4) Price protection notice: Redwood will provide 60 days notice for list changes. Any changes will not affect committed volumes within the protection period.

I'll prepare a short one-page commercial summary and a redline SOW for your review. Rafael (cc) can help with an expedited legal review if Nimbus procurement sends redlines back.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
